exercise1.prompt: inventory of apples, bananas and oranges; get() apples and get() grapes with a default of 0

hiddenCases.name: get('grapes', 0) falls back to the default
asking about grapes did not add grapes

exercise1.hint: Square brackets on a missing key stop the program. get() is the version that hands back a default instead, and the default is the second argument.

exercise2.prompt: scores for Alice, Bob and Charlie; loop with items() printing "Name: Score"

cases.name: each name and score on its own line

exercise2.hint: Looping over a dictionary on its own gives you keys and nothing else. items() is what hands you the key and the value together, so the loop can unpack two names at once.

questions.prompt: What does for x in scores: give you on each pass?
questions.explain: Iterating a dictionary walks its keys. That is why for name, score in scores: fails and for name, score in scores.items(): works.

questions.prompt: Match each dictionary method to what it hands back.
questions.explain: The first three are views over the whole dictionary; get() answers about one key and is the only one that takes a fallback.

questions.prompt: inventory.get("grapes") on a dictionary with no grapes returns what?
questions.explain: With no default supplied, get() returns None. If you want 0, you have to say so: inventory.get("grapes", 0).

questions.prompt: for name, score in scores.___(): unpacks each pair as the loop runs.
questions.explain: items() yields a two-item tuple each time round, and the two loop variables unpack it.
